issues.legal_issue: A mortgage term stating that the property becomes an absolute transfer if the debt is not repaid within the specified period makes the mortgagee the absolute owner under the instrument if that term is enforceable.
material_facts: The deed required repayment within a specified period and stated that after that period the shop would be an absolute transfer, leaving the mortgagor no further say.
Neither the mortgagor nor the mortgagor’s heir repaid the debt within the specified period.
issues.conclusion: On the deed’s terms, non-payment within the specified period would extinguish the mortgagor’s title and make the mortgagee the absolute owner.
issues.legal_principle: The deed must be read as a whole and in context. The phrase indicating that the mortgagor would have no further say in the property after the specified period meant that the mortgagor would lose title and the mortgagee would become its absolute owner, if the deed’s terms prevailed.

predicates.mortgage_redemption_proceeding: A claimant seeks redemption of property held by a mortgagee.
predicates.instrument_makes_property_absolute_trans: The mortgage instrument states that the property will become an absolute transfer to the mortgagee if the debt is not repaid by the stated deadline.
predicates.debt_unpaid_at_deadline: The mortgagor and any successor do not repay the debt by the stated deadline.

issues.definition: When a redemption proceeding concerns an instrument that makes the property an absolute transfer after non-payment, and the debt remains unpaid at the deadline, the mortgagee acquires absolute title under the instrument.

issues.legal_issue: The equitable protection of the right to redeem applies to a mortgage containing a term that restricts redemption even where the applicable property-transfer statute does not govern the transaction.
material_facts: The mortgage deed provided that the mortgagee would become the absolute owner if the debt was not repaid within the specified period, a restriction on the mortgagor’s right to redeem.
The property was in a territory where the Transfer of Property Act did not apply when the mortgage was made or when the repayment period expired.

The Court found that courts in India had consistently applied equitable principles against unreasonable restrictions on redemption, and that no material established that those principles were irrelevant in the territory concerned.
issues.conclusion: The equitable principle applied despite the non-application of the Transfer of Property Act; the restrictive term could not bar the claim for redemption, subject to the general law of limitation.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the general equitable principle underlying section 60 of the Transfer of Property Act, including the mortgagor’s right to redeem, and on provisions directing courts to decide according to justice, equity and good conscience. It relied on Namdeo Lokman Lodhi v. Narmadabai for the proposition that courts apply those principles even where the Act does not apply; on the established practice of the Madras and Bombay High Courts against enforcing oppressive restrictions on redemption; and on the Rajasthan High Court decisions in Amba Lal v. Amba Lal and Seleh Raj v. Chandan Mal, as well as Nainu v. Kishan Singh. The Court distinguished the Privy Council decisions in Pattabhiramier v. Vencatarow Naicken, Thumbusawmy Moodelly v. Hossain Rowthen, Kader Moideen v. Nepean, and Mehrban Khan v. Makhna, noting the applicable statutory or established-practice context in those decisions.

rule.if: mortgage_redemption_proceeding and clause_restricts_equity_of_redemption and transfer_statute_inapplicable and equitable_practice_supported

predicates.mortgage_redemption_proceeding: A claimant seeks to redeem property held under a mortgage.
predicates.clause_restricts_equity_of_redemption: The mortgage instrument contains a term that unreasonably restricts the mortgagor’s ability to redeem the property.
predicates.transfer_statute_inapplicable: The statute governing transfers of property does not govern the mortgage transaction.
predicates.equitable_practice_supported: The record supports that courts apply equitable principles to mortgage disputes and contains no material showing that those principles are unavailable.

issues.definition: If a claimant seeks redemption, the mortgage contains an unreasonable restriction on redemption, the property-transfer statute does not govern, and equitable practice is supported, the restriction cannot bar redemption.
